1.why: The reset record stores accountId and verify-reset/update-password enforce claimedBy and mfaVerifiedBy matching the session, so the code is checked against the owning account and session.

2.why: Tokens are created only for the single account and become locked to the first session that verifies them (claimedBy check), so the same code does not work for any other user or session.

3.why: update-password only replaces the hash and marks the reset record used; the sessions map is never invalidated, so any previously authenticated sessions remain valid after a reset.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with a TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, but no explicit TLS protocol version is pinned to guarantee the latest version.

5.why: Reset codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as bcrypt (cost 10), which is appropriate protection, though it is hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: The simulated email is a browser log entry that prints the full reset token and link in plaintext; it contains no other private data but does not guard the token itself.

7.why: All inputs are validated (email regex, password policy, token/code formats, body size cap) and dynamic content is rendered via textContent, though no dedicated sanitization/escaping library is used.

8.why: The reset link is built from location.origin with an encoded token, no user-controlled redirects exist, and CSP enforces form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none'.

9.why: The simulated email is rendered with textContent, all innerHTML templates are static strings, and a strict nonce-based CSP blocks injected scripts.

10.why: Error responses are generic with no stack traces, but the logs panel and console explicitly display the reset token and MFA code in plaintext.

11.why: Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes, but the initial password 'Initial!Passw0rd2025' and the MFA code '246810' are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: The system seeds the account with a hardcoded, source-visible initial password, which functions as a default credential.

13.why: Throttles exist (3 reset requests, 5 verify, 5 MFA, 5 login attempts per window) plus a 15-minute account lockout after 5 failed logins, though session-based limits reset with a new session cookie.

14.why: Reset and login responses are generic and a mock token is returned for every reset request, though login timing differs slightly because bcrypt verify only runs for the matching email.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte CSPRNG tokens, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, single-use, 15-minute expiry, and bound to the account and claiming session.
